Meet the people on your side

ISA is more than an agency. It is a family that walks beside you as you build your future.

Dona Taguinod-Leach

Founder and Managing Director

From humble beginnings in the Philippines to building a life and career in Australia, Dona has guided countless students toward their dreams.

Read Dona's story

She understands the hopes, challenges and sacrifices that come with starting a new life in another country, and has dedicated herself to making that transition smoother for every student she supports.

Her deep knowledge of the Australian and New Zealand education systems, combined with her warm and approachable style, turns uncertainty into confidence. For Dona, ISA is a mission to give back, open doors and create opportunities.

Emelynne Agcaoili

Country Manager

A certified international education consultant (ICEF, QEAC No. 13388) with over 37 years of leadership experience in education.

Read Emelynne's story

A retired Education Program Supervisor from the Department of Education in the Philippines, Emelynne has worked as a teacher, principal and supervisor. In 2002 she was honoured nationally as the Most Outstanding School Paper Adviser of the Philippines.

At ISA she guides students through program selection, strong applications, visa processes and preparing for life abroad.

Questions we hear a lot

Can't find yours? Call or message us and we will answer it.

Does it cost anything to apply through ISA?

No. There is no application fee when you apply through us.

What does the free visa chat cover?

A free 15-minute consultation with licensed migration agents, so you understand the requirements before you apply.

Can I talk to you if I'm still overseas?

Yes. Virtual counselling is available, and you can book an appointment, chat online or call.

Do you help with New Zealand as well as Australia?

Yes. We guide students toward study in both countries.

What happens after I arrive?

We stay in touch through your studies, then help with internships, job placements and further study.

Can I get a scholarship?

Many universities offer scholarships to international students, either merit-based or need-based. Ask us, and check with your institution before you borrow.

Crossing rivers, building bridges

In the rural villages of Cagayan Valley, a young girl crossed rivers barefoot every day to get to school, carrying her books and lunch above her head. That girl was Dona Taguinod Leach, and the resilience she learned then became a mission to help others cross their own rivers of hardship.

When the pandemic left many Filipino students without family income and out of school, Dona, by then living in Australia, decided to act. In 2021 she launched the ISA Scholarship Program through ISA Australia. It began with five students in partnership with the Department of Education.

Today it combines financial aid, mentorship, pastoral care and leadership development, so students stay in school and thrive. It is not charity. It is a bridge, built on resilience, compassion and shared responsibility between schools, families and communities.

“Every scholar represents a dream rekindled, a future reshaped, and a community one step closer to upliftment.”
Dona Taguinod Leach, Founder and Managing Director

A 10-point policy framework

It turns the program from financial aid into a shared responsibility between schools, families, communities and alumni, with safeguards built in.

  1. 1

    Fair and transparent selection

    Students are chosen through a clear, merit-based process that balances academic ability with financial need, so scholarships go to students who are both high-achieving and genuinely underprivileged.

  2. 2

    Structured mentorship by educators

    Principals and teachers act as formal mentors, with regular check-ins that cover schoolwork, life skills and encouragement.

  3. 3

    Safeguards against misuse of funds

    School leaders sign agreements that scholarship funds are used only for the student's education.

  4. 4

    Parent and guardian partnership

    Families agree in writing that stipends cover school needs such as transport, uniforms, meals and learning materials, and take part in the scholar's pastoral care.

  5. 5

    Community validation

    Local community leaders issue a Certificate of Indigency to confirm a student's financial hardship.

  6. 6

    Ongoing monitoring and term reports

    Each term, students and mentors report on academic performance, school activities and any challenges, so ISA can step in early.

  7. 7

    Development and leadership plans

    Each scholar builds a personal academic and leadership plan with their mentor, with measurable goals.

  8. 8

    Program accountability and transparency

    ISA publishes annual reports on scholar progress, fund allocation and overall impact.

  9. 9

    Alumni and peer mentorship

    Graduated scholars stay connected as peer mentors and role models for the next generation.

  10. 10

    Holistic well-being and safeguarding

    Mentoring includes checks on emotional health, safety and personal development, with referrals to support services when needed.

Student spotlight

Stories from the scholars and partners of the ISA Scholarship Program.

3 May 2024, Peñablanca, CagayanFirst scholar: Aldwin Jeam T. Mueco

ISA Australia and MCNP–ISAP sign an agreement to launch a scholarship program

ISA Australia partnered with the Medical Colleges of Northern Philippines and the International School of Asia and the Pacific to provide full scholarships to academically promising students facing financial hardship.

The first recipient is Aldwin Jeam T. Mueco, a Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management student at ISAP, chosen for his academic performance, class participation and leadership. Dona Taguinod-Leach and MCNP–ISAP President Dr Christian Guzman both committed to supporting students with guidance as well as funding.

A question about pain that became a calling

Resilience grows where roots run deep

From the rice fields of Dungeg to Sta. Teresita National High School, Godly Kate is the eldest daughter of a farmer and a homemaker. She balances housework, farm life and school, and keeps a consistent honor record.
